rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance
rules.requirement: Jersey City regulates rents in buildings with 5 or more units under its Rent Control Ordinance, administered by the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations. All 1-4 unit properties are exempt, and owners may request other permitted exemptions.
rules.key_value: Rent control for 5+ unit properties; 1-4 unit exempt
citation_aliases: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260
rules.quoted_span: (Please Note: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control)
rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties; other permitted exemptions via Rent Control Exemption Request; newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt for 30 years under state law

unverifiable_exemptions: other exemptions under the Rent Control Ordinance require an owner exemption request

rules.review_note: The page does not state the cap formula or enactment/effective date. The 30-year new-construction exemption comes from N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5 (state context).

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ordinance is enforced publicly and privately, with fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic rent coordination services; fines up to $2,000 per day
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day
rules.effective_date_note: Law-firm alert states 'effective June 2025'; exact day not given.
rules.conflict_note: NJ FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43, eff. 7/1/2027) may preempt this ordinance once it takes effect; the source documents do not discuss this.

parsed.notes: Merged c82 and c89 (same Morgan Lewis alert, two URLs). No documents cover Jersey City just cause, deposits, fees or screening, so no findings were added. Those categories are governed by NJ state law. Link-only D035 (Hudson County View) likely covers the same RealPage ban and was not needed.
